title: Easy e-Pay: Clearing Income Tax Dues Online

faq.a: Challan 280 is the official receipt generated by the Income Tax Department after you make an online tax payment. It contains essential details like your PAN, the Assessment Year, the type of tax paid, the amount, and a unique Challan Serial Number, all crucial for ITR filing.

faq.q: Can I pay income tax online without logging in to the portal?
faq.a: Yes, you can pay income tax online through the e-Pay Tax service on the Income Tax portal without logging in. You will need to enter your PAN, select the Assessment Year and type of payment, and provide basic contact details.

faq.q: What if I select the wrong Assessment Year or type of payment?
faq.a: Selecting the wrong Assessment Year or payment type can lead to discrepancies and potential tax demands. If this happens, you might need to file a rectification request or contact the Income Tax Department for guidance on how to adjust the payment.

faq.q: Is there a fee for paying income tax online?
faq.a: Generally, there are no additional charges or fees levied by the Income Tax Department for making online tax payments. However, your bank might impose transaction charges depending on the payment method (e.g., credit card processing fees, though rarely applicable for direct tax payments).

faq.q: How long does it take for the payment to reflect in Form 26AS?
faq.a: Typically, an online tax payment reflects in your Form 26AS within 3-4 working days. It is advisable to wait for it to appear before filing your ITR to ensure accurate reconciliation.

faq.q: Can NRIs use the e-Pay facility?
faq.a: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can also use the e-Pay facility on the Income Tax portal to pay their tax dues in India, provided they have a valid PAN. The process remains largely the same.

faq.q: What payment methods are accepted for e-Pay?
faq.a: The e-Pay facility accepts various payment methods including net banking, debit cards, UPI, and RTGS/NEFT. You can also generate a challan to pay at a designated bank counter for certain payment types and amounts.
